4. Mr. Abdul Momin Talukder, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners firstly submits that the allegatic made in the F.I.R. do not constitute a offence against the petitioners and the charge sheet has been wrongly submitted and the charges have also been illegal  framed against the petitioners. As so the proceedings of the case are liable to quashed. The continuation of the said will be an abuse of the process of court. His next submission is that take cognizance of the offence under sec 366 read with the Cruelty to Word (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance and framing charges under sections 366/368 read with Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 are wholly bad illegal and without jurisdiction as because the schedule and the non-schedule offence cannot betrayed together. He, of course raised another point to the effect that accused No. 15 in a nika Registrar and as such a public servant and without prior sanction from the appropriate Government cognizance of the offences against him could not be taken by the Special Tribunal. 

 7. Now, let us consider the second point urged on behalf of the petitioners which appears to be of vital importance in this case at is to the effect that the accused petitioners have been charged under sections 366 and 368 of the Penal Code which are non-schedule offences together with the schedule offence under the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 of course without mentioning any specific section of the same. The latter one is a schedule offence under the Special Powers Act, 1974 exclusively triable by a Special Tribunal. But in the instant case, both the above offences schedule and non-schedule have been joined together and accordingly charges have been framed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal No. 11 by his order dated 29.2.88. This is undoubtedly bad, illegal and without jurisdiction. In support of the above view, a number of decisions have been cited before us by the learned Advocate for the petitioners, namely a decision in the case of Talukder Abdul Aziz Vs. The State reported in 35 D.L.R. (H.C.D) 127 wherein it has been observed as follows:- 

 "The cognizance of the offence in the present case suffers from an inherent initial illegality as the schedule and the non-schedule offences were joined altogether to be tried by the Special Tribunal at one trial whereas the tribunal was constituted only to try cases mentioned in the schedule of the Special Powers Act and not for offences under the ordinary penal laws of the land". 

 'The joinder of schedule offences and non-schedule offences was thus illegal and so also the cognizance taken by the Special Tribunal of both schedule and non-schedule offences were without jurisdiction." 

 8. In another decision in the case of Tamiz Miah alias Tamizuddin Miah vs. Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, reported in 33 D.L.R. 203, it has been observed that, joinder of schedule and non-schedule offences was illegal and the trial by the Special Tribunal for both schedule and non-schedule offences was also without any lawful authority. "Similar view was taken in the case of M.M. Rafiqul Hyder Vs. The State reported in 41 D.L.R. 274 wherein it has been held. 

 "In view of the trend of the decisions of this court as mentioned above we are of the view that the joined of scheduled and non-scheduled offences in the present case vitiated the entire proceedings. The learned Tribunal committed illegality in taking cognizance of the case framing the charge and convicting and sentencing the appellant and it requires interference." 

 9. So, from the above decisions arrived at by this court in different cases, it is absolutely clear in the instant case that the learned Sessions and Special Tribunal No. 1 committed illegality in taking cognizance by his order dated 1.7.88 of both the schedule and non-schedule offences against the accused petitioners and similarly the learned Additional Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal No. II also acted illegal and without jurisdiction in framing charges against the accused petitioners under sections 366/368 of the Penal Code as well as under the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 by his order dated 29.2.88. It is found from the decision 

 cited above that the High Court Division, having found the trial of the schedule and non-schedule offences together by the Special Tribunal to be illegal and without jurisdiction, quashed the proceedings of the cases. 

 10. Mr. Saiful Huq, the learner Advocate for the opposite party No. 2. However, does not dispute the proposition of law and the principles as laid down in the above cases and he frankly concedes that he has no grievance if the impugned order taking cognizance and framing charges under the aforesaid schedule and non-schedule offences against the petitioners are set aside or quashed. His only grievance is that admittedly when there is no illegality in constituting the Special Tribunal which is quite competent to try the schedule offences, namely the offences under the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 elements of which are fully disclosed in the F.I.R. and the charge sheet in the instant case, the Sessions of Additional Sessions Judge as Special Tribunal is quite competent to try the alleged offences under the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983, but is barred from trying the offences under sections 366 and 368 of Penal Code at the same trial and in the same capacity. Hence there is no justification on quashing the entire proceedings of the case allowing the offenders to go scot free without facing the trial. The proceeding so far it relates to the non-schedule offences may however, be quashed but when it is found that the allegations made in the F.I.R. and as well as in the charge sheet disclose a prima facie-case of a schedule offences under the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 read with the Special Powers Act, on a mere technical ground on the question of joint trial offences schedule and non-schedule, the entire proceedings should not be quashed allowing the accused petitioners to avoid their trial and to go unpunished. Mr. Saiful Huq in support of his above contention has relied on a decision in the case of the State Vs. Abdur Rab Mia and another, reported in 1987 B.C.R. (AD) 41. In this case, charge sheet was submitted under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with the Special Powers Act the learned Senior Special Judge who was also a Special Tribunal took cognizance of the offence under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 as a special case but without having prior sanction from the appropriate Government, though the accused was a public servant. The proceeding of the said case was challenged by an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure mainly on the ground that taking cognizance of the offence without prior sanction from appropriate Government was illegal and that the Special Judge had no jurisdiction to try the case. The High Court Division held that taking cognizance of the offence without prior sanction from the Government was illegal and without jurisdiction accordingly quashed the entire proceedings. Against that decision of the High Court Division, the State went in appeal before the Appellate Division the State went in appeal before the Appellate Division mainly on the ground that quashment of the entire proceedings by the High Court Division was illegal.
